correctness.rationale: The 75 classical complex lines and cross-family rank-four incidence equivalences are explicitly defined and proved by coordinate elimination. The finite graph is 18-regular with 675 edges and connected. A standalone standard-library exact checker independently tests all 2775 line-pair 4x4 determinants over F_11, checks an integer spectral annihilator and traces 75,0,1350,2550, and derives tree determinant 2^48*3^37*5^84. Local unimodular operations over Z/(p^(e+1)) recover complete Smith valuations 2:(0^50,2^24),3:(0^37,1^37),5:(0^26,1^25,2^12,3^9,4^2) for three independent reduced Laplacians; sorted factors multiply to that determinant. The symbolic incidence derivation, not the finite-field experiment, justifies the complex input; no characteristic-uniform assertion is made.

originality.rationale: Published full texts [1] and [2] determine the geometric line incidence and surface Picard lattice, not the graph Laplacian Smith form. The closest published all-degree line-graph result establishes the exact spectrum and tree number, explicitly excluding Smith forms from its claims; it therefore implies group order but not cyclic invariant factors. The published Fermat-quartic critical-group calculation is for a different 48-line graph and does not furnish the 75-line decomposition. An exact-characteristic-two Hermitian-quintic line-lattice Smith form uses 325 lines and a 325x325 intersection matrix, not the 75-line graph Laplacian. Repeated published-finding corpus/source/alias/numeric searches found no same-object complete integral graph critical group. Residual historical priority risk remains because the incidence matrix is classical and unindexed computations may exist.
residual_risks: Historical unindexed mathematical or computer-algebra tables could contain this exact Smith form.
The published classical intersection formula makes the proposed matrix reconstructible even without the displayed decomposition; historical priority has not been independently checked.
This is a single natural degree-five case; its value is the integral 5-primary classification rather than a general all-degree theorem.

value.rationale: The 75-line Fermat quintic is the first higher-degree odd classical Fermat-surface line configuration after cubics, on the first degree of smooth hypersurfaces of general type in P^3. Its line classes are known to generate the whole surface Picard lattice. The critical group of their complete and canonical incidence graph is a motivated, intrinsic finite graph-divisor invariant; its complete 5-primary depth (including two 5^4 factors) is not specified by the known spectrum or tree number and illustrates integral information that the rational graph representation omits. No arbitrary slice or renaming of a known table is involved. Scope is deliberately only this mathematically distinguished surface; comparison to quartic and Hermitian configurations supplies context, not an unsupported downstream theorem.
